#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -c 1 -g 2 -t 120h --job-name=test-random-list13 --output=/scratch/yaoy4/log/test-random-list13.log script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 4         : 4 tasks (from --ntasks=4)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (implicit, adjust if needed)
# -g 2         : 2 GPUs total (from --gres=gpu:2)
# -t 120h      : 120 hour walltime (from --time=120:00:00)
# --job-name=test-random-list13 : job name derived from output log filename
# --output=/scratch/yaoy4/log/test-random-list13.log : output file path
#
# Note: Flux combines stdout and stderr by default
# Use --error=<file> separately if stderr redirection is needed

# Original Slurm account: p_masi_gpu
# Slurm: --account=p_masi_gpu
# Note: Flux uses banks/accounts through flux-accounting
# Set at submission if flux-accounting is configured:
# flux batch --setattr=bank=p_masi_gpu ...
# Performance impact: Without bank specification, job runs under default account
# which could affect priority, resource limits, or accounting tracking

# Original Slurm partition: maxwell
# Slurm: --partition=maxwell
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# The 'maxwell' partition likely refers to Maxwell GPU architecture
# Without partition specification, job may be scheduled on any available nodes
# For GPU architecture constraints, consult site-specific Flux configuration
# May need to use --requires or --setattr for GPU type constraints

# GPU allocation: 2 GPUs
# Slurm: --gres=gpu:2
# Flux: -g 2 allocates 2 GPUs total
# Note: GPU type/model cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# The maxwell partition likely ensured Maxwell architecture GPUs
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated different GPU types
# Consult site-specific Flux configuration for GPU property constraints

# Memory: 40GB
# Slurm: --mem=40G (total memory for the job)
# Flux memory specification: --setattr=system.memory=40960M (40 * 1024 MB)
# Note: Memory attribute syntax may vary by Flux version
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory=40960M
# Alternative: --setattr=memory=40960M (verify for your Flux version)
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors

# Tasks: 4
# Slurm: --ntasks=4
# Flux: -n 4 specifies 4 tasks
# Note: The script runs 7 sequential python commands, not parallel tasks
# The --ntasks=4 may have been for resource reservation or intended parallelism
# Consider if -n 4 is actually needed, or if -n 1 would be more appropriate

# Environment setup
# Note: setpkgs is a site-specific package management tool (not standard)
# This may not be available in Flux environment
# Verify availability or replace with appropriate module load command
setpkgs -a tensorflow_0.12

# Run TensorFlow training jobs
# Note: These are sequential executions, not parallel
# The original script runs the same command 7 times sequentially
# Consider if this is intentional or if parallelization was intended
# With --ntasks=4, if parallel execution was intended, use:
# flux run -n 1 -g 1 python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13 &
# (adjust GPU allocation per task as needed)

python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13
python /scratch/yaoy4/BodySegmentation/run.py train random 13

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -c 1 -g 2 -t 120h \
#   --job-name=test-random-list13 \
#   --output=/scratch/yaoy4/log/test-random-list13.log \
#   --setattr=system.memory=40960M \
#   --setattr=bank=p_masi_gpu \
#   script.sh
#
# Note: Adjust resource allocation based on actual parallelization needs
# If running 7 sequential jobs, consider: -n 1 -g 2 (single task, 2 GPUs)
# If running parallel jobs, structure the script accordingly with flux run

reasons: Memory specification is missing from the primary submission command. The documented command 'flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -c 1 -g 2 -t 120h --job-name=test-random-list13 --output=/scratch/yaoy4/log/test-random-list13.log script.sh' does not include the required memory allocation '--setattr=system.memory=40960M' which is documented as necessary.

Resource allocation mismatch: The script allocates 4 tasks (-n 4) but runs 7 sequential Python commands without any parallelization. This creates inefficient resource usage where 3 of the 4 allocated task slots remain unused throughout execution.

GPU allocation ambiguity: With -n 4 tasks and -g 2 GPUs total, the GPU distribution per task is unclear (2 GPUs / 4 tasks = 0.5 GPU per task, which is not possible). The script should either specify -n 1 with -g 2 for sequential execution, or properly distribute GPU resources if parallel execution is intended.
issues: The primary submission command at the top of the script is incomplete and differs from the complete command at the bottom. Users following the top command will have insufficient memory allocation.

The complete submission command at the bottom includes '--setattr=system.memory=40960M' and '--setattr=bank=p_masi_gpu', but these are not in the primary command documentation at the top, creating confusion.

The memory attribute syntax 'system.memory' should be verified. Depending on Flux version, it might need to be just 'memory' or a different attribute path. The script acknowledges this uncertainty but doesn't provide definitive guidance.
The script runs 7 identical sequential commands without any error handling. If one fails, the others continue executing, potentially wasting resources. Consider adding error checking between runs.
The setpkgs command is site-specific and may not work in Flux environments. No fallback or alternative is provided.
No validation that the GPU allocation is successful or that TensorFlow can see the GPUs before starting training.

The script doesn't make use of the 4 allocated tasks. If sequential execution is intended, the resource request should be '-n 1 -g 2'. If parallel execution is desired, the script should be restructured to use 'flux run' or parallel job launching.
The 120-hour time limit is extremely long (5 days). Consider if this is actually necessary or if a shorter time with job chaining would be more appropriate.
No mechanism to track which of the 7 runs completed successfully. All output goes to the same log file, making debugging difficult.
The bank specification '--setattr=bank=p_masi_gpu' is only shown in the complete command example but not emphasized as required if accounting is in use.
